title.en: Identify sequence, selection and repetition in an algorithm

say.en: Every algorithm is built from just three moves: go straight, choose a turn, or go round again. Let us see each one. In this lesson: Identify sequence, selection and repetition in an algorithm.
Write pseudocode with IF over ELSE.
Write pseudocode with WHILE.

body.en: Flow of control is the order in which the steps of an algorithm are executed. In a *sequence*, steps run one after another. In selection, a condition is checked and one of the alternative paths is chosen, as in IF condition THEN … ELSE …. The condition evaluates to TRUE or FALSE. Selection can also check several conditions one after another.

title.en: On the board: Sequence, selection and repetition

say.en: In a sequence the steps simply run one after another.
In selection a condition is checked, and only one path is taken.
In repetition, steps are repeated while a condition stays true. Something must change so that the loop ends.
Trace: sum equals 0 and i equals 1. While i is at most 4, add i to sum and increase i.
When i becomes 5 the condition is false and the loop stops. The sum is 10.

explanation.en: Sequence runs steps one after another, selection chooses a path with a condition, and repetition runs steps again and again while a condition stays true.

body.en: *Repetition* (iteration, or a loop) executes a set of steps again and again while a condition remains true, as in WHILE condition DO …. The loop must change something each time so that the condition eventually becomes false; otherwise it never ends. For example, to add the numbers from 1 to N, a counter goes up by 1 each time until it passes N.

A loop without an exit never ends

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Write pseudocode to print whether a number is odd or even.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Write pseudocode to print whether a number is odd or even.
INPUT number.
IF number MOD 2 == 0 THEN.
PRINT "Even".
ELSE.
PRINT "Odd".
So the answer is For 14 it prints Even; for 7 it prints Odd.

problem.en: Write pseudocode to find the sum of the first N natural numbers and trace it for N = 4.

steps.en: WHILE i <= N DO: sum = sum + i; INCREMENT i
Trace: sum becomes 1, 3, 6, 10 as i goes 1, 2, 3, 4; then i = 5 > 4 and the loop stops.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Write pseudocode to find the sum of the first N natural numbers and trace it for N = 4.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Write pseudocode to find the sum of the first N natural numbers and trace it for N equals 4.
INPUT N; SET sum equals 0, i equals 1.
WHILE i <= N DO: sum equals sum plus i; INCREMENT i.
PRINT sum.
Trace: sum becomes 1, 3, 6, 10 as i goes 1, 2, 3, 4; then i equals 5 is greater than 4 and the loop stops.
So the answer is For N equals 4 the output is 10.
